confirmedDefects.resolution: Exact candidate, product, strategy hash, executor-source hash, evidence checksum, frozen protocol, independently evaluated result, prospectively ordered dates, recomputed acceptance rules, and execution assumptions are enforced before connection and re-verified by the low-level purchase method. Generic order-bearing requests are rejected. The tracked decision contains no candidate and blocks execution.
Account fingerprint and immutable intended terms are journalled; assignment requires exactly one candidate statement row, whose authoritative contract identity and tick/clock terms agree.
Bounded offset pagination now records completeness, detects duplicates/change/failure, and requires two separated complete no-match observations before not_purchased.
One strict validator handles immediate and restart settlement; null, blank, boolean, non-finite, identity-mismatched, inconsistent and unsupported cancellation records remain unresolved.

Every event requires account, strategy and event-time identity; exact initial terms, legal transitions and chronology are checked; settlement requires prior reconciliation; accepted numeric strings are normalized before risk accounting.
Trade counts use UTC entry date; realized P&L uses UTC settlement date; unique corrections use their correction date.
The checkpoint is verified against a separately tracked approved collection specification and cannot redefine the target.
Rejected summary/inventory cross-checks clear intermediate values and all dependent published fields become unverifiable.
Signals require recent contiguous completed candles, proposal terms must be present and agree, and frozen payout and response-time-inclusive quote-age constraints are applied before purchase.

researchAssessment.independentOutcomeClusters: Far fewer than configurations: every configuration used the same 30-day 1HZ100V slice and three UTC window clusters; prior audit found 5,728 distinct outcome-count signatures.
researchAssessment.interpretation: Strong negative development evidence for the tested short-tick directional indicator rules under the frozen assumed payouts; not historical executable-account profitability and not universal Deriv evidence.

rankedDirections.product: RB100/RB200 MULTUP and MULTDOWN multiplier contracts
rankedDirections.horizon: Multi-tick holding across within-range approaches and breaks; no fixed expiry in captured metadata
rankedDirections.mechanism: Deriv documents repeated support/resistance ranges and breaks after an average number of boundary hits.
rankedDirections.dataAvailable: Public ticks and point-in-time entry proposals only
rankedDirections.smallestFalsifier: First obtain a coherent account-applicable specification and a timestamped entry/close valuation feed. Then preregister a small boundary-state diagnostic; raw price-path results alone cannot establish net profit.

rankedDirections.product: Drift Switch 10/20/30 or Volatility Switch CFDs
rankedDirections.horizon: Minutes, shorter than the documented average regime duration
rankedDirections.mechanism: Deriv describes persistent bullish/bearish/sideways or low/medium/high-volatility phases.
rankedDirections.dataAvailable: Product descriptions; no exact local symbol dataset or synchronized executable prices
rankedDirections.smallestFalsifier: A fixed one-proxy state-classification test on synchronized bid/ask data, followed by net CFD simulation only if full costs and margin rules are available.

rankedDirections.product: Skew Step 5 Up/Down; Skew Step 4 deferred
rankedDirections.mechanism: Published asymmetric marginal step probabilities define tail risk; conditional dependence would be a separate, unproven mechanism.
rankedDirections.dataAvailable: Published marginal distributions; no exact local tick/quote dataset or executable-cost history
rankedDirections.smallestFalsifier: Only after specification resolution, preregister one conditional-dependence statistic with simulated independent controls and one correction family; dependence would not itself prove profitability.

decision.reason: None of the three available datasets contains the executable entry/exit economics needed by its product. A midpoint-only backtest would answer the wrong question.
decision.singleNextAction: Resolve RB100 account-applicable product terms and establish a legitimate timestamped entry-and-close valuation source before any strategy search.
decision.continueOnlyIf: Catalog/proposal limits and commission units are coherent, and contract-specific close values, delays and stop-out paths can be captured without hindsight.
decision.stopIf: Those fields remain unavailable or contradictory; do not substitute more indicators or midpoint history.
